title: Book Three · Chapter 191: The Whole Agreement Finished
story:
In April, Ronan completes the last two weeks of his agreement.

Both Friday payments are thirty yuan. The final sixty brings his work envelope to five hundred and nineteen.

He has worked fifteen weeks, thirty hours each week. Four hundred and fifty hours have brought four hundred and fifty yuan.

Mr Sun checks the last date and closes the pay book.

“Thank you for the winter and spring,” he says.

Ronan thanks him too. The counter helper has the next week's papers ready. Dad and the trained workers still have their own jobs.

Before he leaves the counter, Ronan checks the papers in front of him. One reply is finished. Another still needs Mr Sun's answer about a size.

He puts the two apart.

“This one is ready to send,” he tells the counter helper. “This one is waiting.”

She reads the names and moves the unfinished reply to her side of the table.

“I will ask him after the customer goes.”

Ronan nods. He looks around for another job. There are boxes on the shelf and more names in the order book. He starts to reach for the next sheet.

The helper puts her hand on it.

“I have that.”

“Oh. Yes.”

She smiles at him. “You can go home.”

He smiles too. He folds his work cloth and checks that his own papers are in his bag. The shop bell sounds, and she turns to meet the next customer.

Ronan puts the pencil back and carries his cloth home.

At the April household review, Dad adds twelve yuan and Mum eight. Their study envelope now holds two hundred and eighty.

With Ronan's five hundred and nineteen and his older twenty and a half, the actual saved total reaches eight hundred and nineteen and a half.

They sit together with both terms on the sheet.

The two class and room bills total four hundred and eighty at the offered prices. Food for the eight teaching months is an estimate of two hundred and forty.

The present journey to the coast costs twenty. The local arrival bus costs one. Those lines make seven hundred and forty-one.

Ronan writes that below the two terms.

“Not every week of the year,” Mum says.

“No. The weeks outside classes need a plan too.”

They have seventy-eight and a half left beyond those listed costs. It stays a reserve for supplies, food-price changes, and extra journeys.

Mum brings the room-supply sheet. Ronan can take his own blanket and sheets from home. They still need to check the smaller things before packing.

“For a long break, home first?” Dad asks.

“If the dates work,” Ronan says. “We need the break dates before any ticket.”

They leave that question open. No paid practice income goes into the plan.

The first class and room payment of two hundred and forty is still unpaid. It is due at the centre before lessons begin. The second bill will be due before the second teaching term.

Ronan looks at the two school-cost lines. There is money set aside for both, with food estimates beside them.

He puts the sheet away before dinner. Mum keeps the parents' envelope. He takes his two back to his shelf.

Outside, the evening air is warm. Ronan finds his football and rolls it across the yard. Dad stops it by the kitchen step and sends a short pass back before Mum calls them to the table.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

reserve＝留作未定开支的备用钱；teaching month＝实际上课的月份；unpaid＝尚未支付的、没有工资的；packing＝收拾行李。

## 理解问题

1. 十五周真实实付结束、四月实际家存后，各份及合计多少？
2. 七百四十一包含什么、不包含什么？第二学期与剩余备用钱怎样安排，课费已付了吗？

## 读句子

**They sit together with both terms on the sheet.**

拆开看：They / sit together / with both terms / on the sheet.

一家人／坐在一起／把两个学期都列入／同一张计划表中。
